Accessibility
We are dedicated to continually improving our efforts to ensure that all Picklesburgh patrons can enjoy the festival to the fullest. We welcome and encourage your feedback and suggestions. If you have any specific accessibility concerns or questions not addressed on this page, please contact us at pdp@downtownpittsburgh.com.
Wheelchair Access:
Picklesburgh is an outdoor event. The footprint is fully paved and navigable for those with mobility needs. We encourage patrons who require mobility assistance to utilize personal forms of transportation, such as wheelchairs and scooters. At this time, we do not provide wheelchair / scooter services or rentals.
Restrooms:
Throughout the event footprint restrooms can be found at Alleghany Landing, Market Square, Arts Landing and the Beer Garden between Sixth St. and Stanwix St. Restroom areas within the event footprint are equipped with ADA-compliant bathrooms to accommodate all guests. View the festival map
here.
Cooling Misters:
Thank you to
Hymark
for providing cooling misting fans located near the Lil’ Gherkins KidsPlay Area.
Guide Dogs:
Guide dogs and service animals are welcome throughout the event. Please ensure your service animal is easily identifiable.
Parking:
ADA-accessible parking is available at all nearby garages, providing convenient access to the event area. For more information about parking, road closures, and detours,
click here
.
Vendor and Stage Areas:
All vendor areas and stage viewing areas are wheelchair accessible, ensuring that all attendees can access all amenities on the footprint. View the vendor linkeup
here.

text:
Pickle Connoisseurs To Take Downtown By Storm at Picklesburgh – Pittsburgh Magazine’s 2026 ‘Best Of the Burgh’ Food Festival
This one’s for the brine-
iacs
! Picklesburgh – the four-time winner of USA Today’s ‘Best Specialty Food Festival’ contest, and Pittsburgh Magazine’s Food Festival pick for the 2026 Best of the ‘Burgh list – is back for its eleventh year. This year’s festival has the BIGGEST footprint to date, spanning two Sister Bridges (Clemente and Warhol), Allegheny Landing, Allegheny Riverfront Park, Fort Duquesne Boulevard (westbound), PPG Plaza, Sixth Street, Market Square, and the Pittsburgh Cultural Trust’s newly opened Arts Landing. All weekend long, ‘gherkin’ geeks from across the land will enjoy four days of dill-icious food, jar-ring entertainment, and pickle-packed activities.
Picklesburgh returns to a four-day schedule, opening at noon daily from Thursday, July 16, through Sunday, July 19. During the ultimate pickle ex-
spear
-ience, Downtown Pittsburgh will relish in the opportunity to enjoy 55 vendors, 14 Taste of Picklesburgh merchants, exclusive culinary offerings, crowd-rousing Dill-Cathlon contests, a mechanical pickle, live music, KidsPlay activities, pickleball, and the return of the 35-foot-long signature Heinz pickle balloon flying high above the Andy Warhol Bridge.
Created by the Pittsburgh Downtown Partnership (PDP) and presented by HEINZ, Picklesburgh has grown every year since its inception, boosting the Downtown economy and welcoming people from around the country and the world. Picklesburgh 2025 welcomed more than 200,000 people over the course of three days and, according to VisitPittsburgh, brought in an estimated $19.8M in direct spending to the City, which includes overnight lodging, transportation, retail, and recreation, generating over $970,000 in sales tax revenue. “This year’s festival is our biggest one yet, with an expanded footprint from the North Shore to PPG Plaza, welcoming the recently completed Arts Landing” said Jeremy Waldrup, president and CEO of the Pittsburgh Downtown Partnership.
“Picklesburgh is Pittsburgh at its best, creative, welcoming, and a little quirky. For eleven years, this festival has united people from around the region and is special because of the remarkable chefs, makers, musicians, and small businesses that make our city one of a kind. We can’t wait to welcome everyone Downtown for our biggest celebration of community yet.”
“For HEINZ, pickles are in our DNA, so being part of Picklesburgh for more than a decade has been a true
dill-ight
,” said Jamie Mack, Associate Director, Brand Communications at HEINZ. “From our Pickle Relish to our Pickle Ketchup, we’re proud to offer something for every pickle lover. And with an even bigger footprint this year in our hometown of Pittsburgh, we’re excited to show up in a bigger way and celebrate the roots that connect us, both to pickles and to this city.”
NEW: PICKLEBALL MAKES IT DEBUT AT ARTS LANDING
This year, Pickleball joins the festival lineup in the expanded footprint at Arts Landing. The brand-new painted Pickleball courts feature the public artwork
Geometry of Play
created by Sharmistha Ray and commissioned by the Pittsburgh Cultural Trust. Tournaments, beginner-friendly clinics, demonstrations, and learn-to-play sessions will be presented by the Pickleball Warehouse at select times every day during the festival.
View the full Pickleball schedule and learn how to sign up for a clinic at
picklesburgh.com/pickleball
DILLS, THRILLS, AND SPILLS
Presented by the PDP and Flyspace Productions, Pickle Riding made its debut during last year’s festival. This one-of-a-kind activation is Picklesburgh’s take on the classic mechanical bull. Riders will try their best to hang on for ‘dill’ life after pausing to snap a photo on the iconic ‘Briny Buckaroo’. Tickets can be purchased on site. Patrons must be at least 18 years old to ride, but all are welcome to relish the action from the sidelines.
Get all the Pickle Riding details here:
picklesburgh.com/pickleriding
DILL-CATHLON BRINGS BEST & BRINIEST TO COMPETE FOR GHERKIN GLORY!
Hosted by Rachael and John from the YaJagoff! Podcast, the Games include the return of Pickle Juice Drinking, Pickle Eating, and Bobbing for Pickles. Join fellow pickle-pushers at PPG Plaza to cheer on competitors during a preview round on Thursday, July 16, followed by preliminary heats on Friday, July 17, and Saturday, July 18, culminating in championships on Sunday, July 19. The winning champion of each event will relish their victory with $500 in grand prize money, a life-like pickle trophy, and—most importantly—the coveted title of Duke/Duchess of Drinking, Earl/Countess of Eating, or Baron/Baroness of Bobbing.
“As lifelong Pittsburgh fans, there’s nothing better than joining thousands of fellow pickle lovers Downtown,” said Rachael Rennebeck and John Chamberlin of YaJagoff! Media. “We can’t wait to soak up the fun, the flavor, and maybe a little pickle juice at Picklesburgh!”
The PDP is excited to welcome Club Wingstop as the primary sponsor of the 2026 Dill-Cathlon Games. In addition to Pickle Juice Drinking sponsor, the Pittsburgh Pickle Company; Pickle Eating Contest sponsor, Clean Express Auto Wash; and Bobbing for Pickles sponsor, Pella.
See the Dill-Cathlon schedule here:
picklesburgh.com/games

Voted the #1 Food Festival in America four times; Picklesburgh is known for its endless offerings of local, national, and international eats and beverages served with a briny spin. Enjoy culinary creations from Copper Coast Confections, DiAnoia’s Eatery, Gosia’s Pierogies, Grill My Dill, Millie’s Ice Cream, Mancini’s, Yuzu Kitchen, and others.
PLUS, sample exclusive items made just for Picklesburgh, such as:
IC Pickle:
Iron City Beer’s pickle-flavored IC Light beer, developed with Pittsburgh Pickle Company, offers a dill-ightfully cool cucumber taste.
Turner’s Pickled Iced Tea:
Coined as the “Official Iced Tea of Picklesburgh,” this limited-edition pickle-flavored iced tea joins Turner’s line-up of classic summer refreshments.
Mancini’s:
The 100-year-old establishment is offering up their classic pepperoni roll, the return of the PGH Roll with Isaly’s ham, Heinz pickles, and Lamagna cheese, and the new Pittsburgh Pierogi roll with pickles.
Jenny Lee’s:
Jenny Lee, The Baker Family is coming to Picklesburgh, bringing fan-favorite sweet and savory swirl breads and a grilled cheese-and-gherkin sandwich.
Wingstop’s Dill Pickle Wings:
This limited-time-only Dill Pickle Dry Rub brings a bold, tangy, and zesty dill pickle flavor to Wingstop’s freshly cooked wings.

For some low-cost pickle-themed carnival games, bring the kiddos to the Li’l Gherkins KidsPlay area in Arts Landing, presented by Edgar Snyder & Associates, which operates until 10 p.m. on Thursday, Friday, Saturday, and until 6 p.m. Sunday. Carnival games including pickle jar toss, pickle bean bag toss, and other fan-favorites are $2 per play. Game tickets can be purchased onsite—no reservation needed. Plus, little ones can enjoy the brand-new public playground at Arts Landing, featuring modern custom wooden structures and engaging play elements.
“Picklesburgh has become a beloved Pittsburgh tradition, and we’re excited to help make it even more memorable for local families. At Edgar Snyder & Associates, we’re proud to sponsor the Kids Area because we believe some of the best community memories are made when children can play, and families can enjoy time together. We’re honored to be part of an event that brings our community together year after year.”
Learn more about the Li’l Gherkins KidsPlay area here:
picklesburgh.com/festivalschedule/lil-gherkins-activity-area

Picklesburgh will offer four days of live music on the stage at Arts Landing, presented by Turner’s. “Turner’s is ready to relish in our 4th year as the Official Iced Tea of Picklesburgh!” said Adriana Mazzotta, Marketing Manager for Turner’s. We’re bringing back our fan favorite, Pickled Iced Tea, made with Picklelixir from our friends at Pittsburgh Pickle Co. We can’t wait for another dill-ightful weekend!”
The stage will be programmed throughout the festival with a diverse range of genres and local favorites including Z-town Street Band, Come September, Clyde’s Electric Chalkboard, NASH.V.ILL, The Polkamaniacs, Aristotle Jones, Pickup Line, and others, along with up-and-coming headliners from Point Park University’s Pioneer Records.

picklesburgh.com/entertainment

picklesburgh.com/vendors

Savor the flavors of Picklesburgh while supporting Downtown businesses during ‘Taste of Picklesburgh’, running now through the festival duration. Discover inventive, pickle-inspired specials offered by thirteen Downtown restaurants and one retailer, including innovative food and drink items and festive apparel. Get a glimpse of all the gherkin goodness here:
picklesburgh.com/taste-of-picklesburgh

As Picklesburgh enters its eleventh year, it continues to garner local and international attention. Brine & Dine: ‘Taste Of Picklesburgh’ Returns Downtown Ahead Of 11th Festival
Early kickoff invites visitors to sample pickle-inspired creations from 14 Downtown businesses, extending the festival’s economic impact across the city.
Get ready for more “dill-lightful” moments as Downtown Pittsburgh relishes an early taste of one of its most anticipated summer traditions.
The Pittsburgh Downtown Partnership (PDP) today announced the return of ‘
A Taste of Picklesburgh’,
launching July 9 and running throughout the 11th Anniversary of Picklesburgh (July 16–19). The event welcomes thirteen Downtown restaurants and one retailer, each offering inventive, pickle-inspired specials that bring some briny bravado and gherkin glee back to the Golden Triangle.
Designed as a pickle-infused preview to the main event, A Taste of Picklesburgh expands the festival footprint beyond its usual core -driving foot traffic, supporting small businesses, and giving visitors more reasons to explore the neighborhood before and during the four-day celebration.
“Picklesburgh has evolved into more than a festival, it’s become a powerful economic engine for Downtown,” said Jeremy Waldrup, President & CEO of the Pittsburgh Downtown Partnership. “What’s exciting about Taste of Picklesburgh is how it spreads that energy throughout the neighborhood. You are seeing downtown business owners find unique and creative ways to tap into the moment and turn it into real opportunity.”
A Growing Economic Force
Over the past decade, Picklesburgh has scaled into a nationally recognized event, drawing more than 200,000 attendees last year—an increase of over 1,000% since its debut in 2015. According to VisitPITTSBURGH, the 2025 festival generated about $20 million in direct visitor spending across lodging, dining, transportation, and retail, along with just under $1 million in sales tax revenue.
A Taste of Picklesburgh builds on that momentum by encouraging earlier and broader engagement with Downtown businesses—turning a long weekend into a multi-day economic driver.
“We are so excited to be included in this year’s Taste of Picklesburgh line-up,” says Nathan Bryner, owner of Cocky’s Coop. “Since opening in Market Square this past March, we have been looking for even more ways to attract Downtown visitors and our inclusion in this event will directly support those efforts. Our specialty items include the Cocky’s Big Dill chicken sandwich, chicken wings with house made dill pickle ranch, and fried pickles!”
A Citywide Flavor
In addition to Cocky’s Coop, this year’s lineup features a wide range of Downtown favorites, including Alta Via Market Square, City Works Eatery & Pour House, Howl at the Moon, Las Velas, Olive or Twist, Original Oyster House, Pizzaiolo Primo, Primanti Bros, Redbeard’s, Revel, Space Bar, and Spritzery, alongside specialty retailer Heinz Healey’s offering limited-time pickle-inspired apparel. Picklesburgh

Pickleball
will join the festival lineup at Arts Landing, the Pittsburgh Cultural Trust’s four-acre outdoor space located in the heart of Downtown. The brand-new painted Pickleball courts will feature commissioned public artwork created specifically for Arts Landing and feature tournaments, beginner-friendly clinics, demonstrations, and learn-to-play sessions presented by the Pickleball Warehouse offered at select times every day during the festival.
“We’ve been asked for years to incorporate pickleball into Picklesburgh and with the investments in Arts Landing, we can finally make it happen!” says Jeremy Waldrup, PDP President and CEO. “Implementing Pickleball into the festival footprint is a great way to continue to grow and evolve the festival but more importantly, these new courts are the latest amenity for the public to enjoy for years and years to come, these investments are exactly what we need to continue to see in Downtown.”
The PDP is proud to be partnering with the Pickleball Warehouse and supporting their efforts to bring this dynamic sport to Downtown Pittsburgh.
“People often ask if Pickleball has anything to do with pickles — and this weekend, it does,” says Warehouse owner Alexa Gervasi. “We’re bringing clinics, tournaments, open play, and a lot of friendly competition. If you’ve been curious about the fastest-growing sport in America, there’s no better way to try it.”
The Cultural Trust commissioned artist Sharmistha Ray to create a vibrant ground mural for Arts Landing’s new pickleball courts, marking the first installation of its kind in the region. Titled
Geometry of Play
, the work is among 23 pieces by 10 artists featured in the Cultural Trust’s inaugural public art program for Arts Landing.
“Arts Landing is all about bringing people together Downtown,” said Kendra Whitlock Ingram, President & CEO of the Pittsburgh Cultural Trust. “There’s no better time to welcome the community to our new pickleball courts than during Picklesburgh. We’re grateful to the Pittsburgh Downtown Partnership for making Arts Landing a key part of this year’s festival experience.”
Painted directly onto the playing surface,
Geometry of Play
transforms the courts into a dynamic visual landscape, merging the logic of game design with the fluidity of abstract painting. Interlocking patterns of circles, triangles, and grids reference kaleidoscopic mandalas and architectural ornamentation while playfully echoing the rules and rhythms of the game itself. As players move across the court, the mural creates a constantly shifting visual and physical experience.
Following Picklesburgh, the Pickleball courts will remain open for public use. A full schedule of summer activities is available at
